articleTitle: RBMK safety study-identifying the measures needed for improvement
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Eastern European Nuclear Power Plant Standards (Digest No: 1996/046)
abstract: A major international RBMK safety review project managed by AEA technology and funded by the CEC TACIS Programme, and the governments of Canada, Sweden and Finland is assessing the safety of RBMK reactors as operated in Russia, Lithuania and Ukraine. RBMK reactors have been the subject of numerous other safety studies by other eastern and western European organisations and Canada. Their objectives were, by necessity, not consistent (for example, identifying the deficiencies, reviewing and assessing the safety, checking the existing safety reports, establishing western style safety justifications). However, they share a common technical content in many areas. As a result a considerable number of safety recommendations have already been published. The problem is to categorise and evaluate these recommendations.

articleTitle: I&C upgrade measures for VVER model V213 units in the Czech Republic, Hungary and Slovakia
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Eastern European Nuclear Power Plant Standards (Digest No: 1996/046)
abstract: NNC have been involved in the first two phases of PHARE project EC/ENE15 for the upgrade of the I&C on three VVER model V213 nuclear power plants in the Czech Republic, Hungary and Slovakia. The terms of reference for this work were: to establish the technical and other reasons for replacement of the I&C; to develop an outline design intent, programme and budget cost; to prepare the technical specifications for the upgraded I&C systems; and to prepare other documents to support the enquiry process for the I&C upgrade. This paper draws on the work undertaken by NNC, briefly describing the plants, their operational history, the reasons for upgrading and the upgrades initiated to date. It then considers some of the constraints and technical difficulties, decisions to be taken and preparatory work required for the early stages of implementation.

articleTitle: Summary of presentation on business prospects, practice and problems in Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Eastern European Nuclear Power Plant Standards (Digest No: 1996/046)
abstract: Since Chernobyl and, more particularly, since the break up of the Soviet Union, the problems of ensuring nuclear safety in Soviet designed nuclear power plant have focused the minds of Western specialists. The author discusses the following aspects of this situation: the need for assistance, soft assistance, funding and other agencies, range of business opportunities, partnerships, nuclear liability, and practical problems.

articleTitle: Ignalina Nuclear Power Plant: implementation of safety upgrades at Ignalina RBMK-project management view
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Eastern European Nuclear Power Plant Standards (Digest No: 1996/046)
abstract: This paper describes the work being undertaken at Ignalina NPP on the Ignalina 1 and 2 Nuclear Safety Project using funds managed by the Nuclear Safety Account of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD). The background of the Nuclear Safety Account and the grants made from it are summarised. Finally, the work of the Project Management Unit (PMU) is described and lessons learned are outlined.

articleTitle: The Multifunctional Simulator Project for improving VVER NPP operator training
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Eastern European Nuclear Power Plant Standards (Digest No: 1996/046)
abstract: One of the many projects funded by European Commission under its PHARE and TACIS technical assistance programme, and targeted at improved nuclear safety at Eastern Europe nuclear power plants is the Multifunctional Simulator Project. Nuclear Electric is one of the contractors involved in the project. Their role is the project management of the project on behalf of EC. The author describes the background to the project, project strategy, and progress to date. The multifunctional simulator concept and its hardware and software are discussed.

articleTitle: A WANO overview of safety improvement measure-achievements to date [nuclear power plants]
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Eastern European Nuclear Power Plant Standards (Digest No: 1996/046)
abstract: This paper reviews the major RBMK nuclear power plant modifications completed by the Russians shortly after the Chernobyl accident in 1986, looks at the major design safety aspects of each of the WWER series of reactors and presents views on the current status and issues associated with the aid programmes to the former Soviet Union and Central and Eastern Europe.
